questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Prolific
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Productive."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Prolific"** means producing a large amount of something. ((विशेषतः लेखक, कलाकार आदि) प्रचुर मात्रा में कृतियों की रचना करने वाला; बहुसर्जक, बहुकृतिक)

 
 
• **Example**: *She is a **prolific**__ goal scorer.*
 
 
 
• **"Productive"** means being able to produce a lot of something. (उत्‍पादित या उत्‍पन्‍न करने वाला (विशेषतः बड़े परिणाम में); उत्‍पादनकारी)
 __
 
• **Example**: *The company wants to sell off its less **productive**__ factories.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, **'Prolific' **and **'Productive'** are synonyms.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: Lazy** means (used about a person) not wanting to work. ((व्‍यक्ति) जो काम न करना चाहे; आलसी, कामचोर)
 
• **Option 3: Unproductive** means not producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities. (बड़ी मात्रा में वस्तुओं, फसलों या अन्य वस्तुओं का उत्पादन या उत्पादन करने में सक्षम नहीं होना)
 
• **Option 4: Unsuccessful **means not successful; not achieving what you wanted to. (असफल, विफल; वांछित वस्‍तु की प्राप्ति में असमर्थ)

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Anger
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Fury.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Anger" **is a feeling of strong displeasure or hostility towards someone or something, while **"fury"** is an intense and often uncontrollable anger or rage.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Anger: She tried to suppress her **anger **when her colleague took credit for her work.
 
• Fury: The athlete was filled with **fury **when he learned that he was disqualified from the competition due to a technicality.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Explanation of the other options:
 
• **Pleasure:** This word does not have a similar meaning to "anger". "Pleasure" means a feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction, and its opposite could be displeasure or dissatisfaction.
 
 
• Example: The children derived great **pleasure **from playing in the park.
 
 
 
• **Comfort: **This word does not have a similar meaning to "anger". "Comfort" means a feeling of relief or consolation, and its opposite could be discomfort or distress.
 
 
• Example: The doctor's reassuring words brought **comfort **to the patient.
 
 
 
• **Agony: **This word is not a synonym of "anger", but it is more closely related to it than the other options. "Agony" means extreme physical or emotional pain, and it can sometimes be a result of intense anger.
 
 
• Example: She was in **agony **after hearing the news of her father's death.

questions.question:
Directions: Each item in this section consists of a sentence with an underlined word followed by four words/groups of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly. 

The team's** __tenacious__**__ __effort led to their victory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **determined**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"tenacious"** means holding fast; characterized by keeping a firm hold; persistent, stubborn, or obstinate. (दृढ़)

 
 
• **Example: **Her tenacious grip on the rope saved her from falling.
 
 
 
• **"Determined"** refers to having made a firm decision and being resolved not to change it; showing determination. (दृढ़ निश्चयी)
 
 
• **Example: **Despite the challenges, she remained determined to complete her studies.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'tenacious'** is closest to **'determined'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **determined**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Lazy** (आलसी): Unwilling to work or use energy.

 
 
• **Example:** He is too lazy to clean his room.
 
 
 
• **Indifferent** (उदासीन): Having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned.
 
 
• **Example: **She was indifferent to the outcome of the game.
 
 
 
• **Weak** (कमजोर): Lacking the power to perform physically demanding tasks; lacking strength or power.
 
 
• **Example:** After the illness, he felt too weak to get out of bed.

Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The media, these days, constructs _______ (misleading) narratives on politics and celebrities to increase the viewership.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"misleading"** means giving the wrong idea or impression, often on purpose. (भ्रामक)

 
 
• **Example: **The advertisement was criticized for being **misleading** and deceptive.
 
 
 
• **"Mendacious"** refers to someone who is not telling the truth; habitually lying. (झूठा)
 
 
• **Example: **The **mendacious** politician was finally exposed for his lies.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **mendacious**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Sincere** (ईमानदार): Free from pretense or deceit; proceeding from genuine feelings.

 
 
• **Example:** Her sincere apology was appreciated by everyone.
 
 
 
• **True** (सत्य): In accordance with fact or reality.
 
 
• **Example: **The statement he made was true and verifiable.
 
 
 
• **Candid** (स्पष्टवादी): Truthful and straightforward; frank.
 
 
• **Example:** She gave a candid interview about her experiences.
